newsitem.title: USA: Possible buyers decline comment on Disney unit bid.
newsitem.headline: Possible buyers decline comment on Disney unit bid.

text.p: Two possible buyers of the Kansas City Star newspaper declined to comment Wednesday on whether they were interested in buying it and other publishing properties owned by Walt Disney Co.
Times Mirror Co and Knight-Ridder Inc were among four companies that sent representatives to tour the offices of the Kansas City Star this week, the newspaper reported on Wednesday.
"We won't comment on any possible acquisitions or divestitures," said Polk Laffoon, a spokesman for Knight Ridder.
But Laffoon did acknowledge that representatives of Knight-Ridder had toured the newspaper's offices this week.
Vicki Cho Estrada, a spokeswoman for Times Mirror, said she could not comment on possible acquisitions. She also declined to comment on whether the company had sent a delegation to visit the Star.
Representatives of the two other companies named in the Star's story, Tribune Co and Hearst Corp, were not immediately available to comment.
Disney said in January that it would explore options related to the publishing operations of Capital Cities/ABC, including a possible sale of the business.

Industry analysts said Disney's publishing assets, which include a variety of newspapers and industry publications such as Women's Wear Daily, Automotive Marketing and Institutional Investor, could fetch as much as $2.5 billion.
